concepts.title: Types of Motion
concepts.definition: The classification of how an object moves, which can indeed be along a straight path, in a circular loop, or repeating periodically over regular intervals.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Motion can be linear, circular, or oscillatory depending on the path traced by the moving body.
question_patterns: classify the motion of the hands of an athlete in a race
what type of motion is shown by a pendulum
classify the motion of a train on a straight bridge
identify the type of motion for a child on a swing

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the object moves along a straight line (rectilinear), in a circle (circular), or back and forth about a mean position (oscillatory/periodic).

concepts.title: Average Speed
concepts.definition: The total distance covered by a moving object divided by the total duration of time taken to cover that distance.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Speed represents the speed with which distance is covered per unit of time.
question_patterns: calculate the speed of the train
find the average speed of a car covering a distance of
what is the speed of an object that travels
how fast is a vehicle moving if it covers

solution_steps.explain: Divide the total distance covered by the total time taken.

concepts.title: Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion
concepts.definition: Uniform motion occurs when an object travels along a straight line at a constant speed, whereas non-uniform motion occurs when its speed changes over time.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Constant speed along a straight line signifies uniform motion, while varying speed signifies non-uniform motion.
question_patterns: distinguish between uniform and non-uniform motion
is a car moving with changing speed in uniform motion
what does a straight line distance-time graph indicate about motion

solution_steps.explain: If the speed remains constant, the motion is uniform. If the speed varies, the motion is non-uniform.

concepts.title: Time Period of a Simple Pendulum
concepts.definition: In brief, the duration of time required by a simple pendulum to complete one full back-and-forth oscillation.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, the time period is determined by dividing the total measured time by the total number of oscillations completed.
question_patterns: calculate the time period of the pendulum
what is the time period if a pendulum takes
find the time taken for one oscillation of a pendulum

solution_steps.explain: Divide the total time taken by the number of oscillations completed.

concepts.title: Distance Covered
concepts.definition: The total length of path traversed by an object moving at a given speed over a specific interval of time.
concepts.key_idea: Distance is the object's result of multiplying the both speed and the time duration of its travel.
question_patterns: calculate the distance between
how far does a car travel in
find the distance covered by a bicycle moving at

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the speed by the time taken.

concepts.title: Time Taken
concepts.definition: The duration required for an object to cover a specific distance while moving at a constant speed.
concepts.key_idea: Time taken is calculated by dividing the total distance by the constant speed of travel.
question_patterns: how much time does a train take to cover
calculate the time taken to travel
find the time duration for a journey of

solution_steps.explain: Divide the distance by the speed.

concepts.title: Speed Unit Conversion
concepts.definition: The process of converting a speed value from kilometers per hour (km/h) to meters per second (m/s) or vice versa.
concepts.key_idea: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 1000 and divide by 3600 (or multiply by 5/18).
question_patterns: convert speed from km/h to m/s
express the speed in m/s
what is the speed in meters per second

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the speed in km/h by 1000 to convert kilometers to meters, and divide by 3600 to convert hours to seconds.

concepts.title: Odometer Distance and Speed
concepts.definition: Calculating the distance traveled using the difference between final and initial odometer readings, and subsequently finding the speed.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, the odometer measures cumulative distance; subtracting the initial reading from the final reading gives the trip's distance.
question_patterns: calculate the distance moved using odometer readings
find the speed of the car from odometer readings
what is the distance covered if the odometer reading changes from

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the initial odometer reading from the final odometer reading.
Divide the calculated distance by the elapsed time.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A simple pendulum takes {total_time} s to complete {oscillations} oscillations. What is the time period of the pendulum?

solution_template.explain: Divide the total time taken by the number of oscillations.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The distance between two stations is {distance} km. A train takes {time} hours to cover this distance. Calculate the speed of the train.

extracted_variables.time: time taken to travel the distance

solution_template.explain: Divide the distance by the time taken.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Salma takes {time_minutes} minutes from her house to reach her school on a bicycle. If the bicycle has a speed of {speed} m/s, calculate the distance between her house and the school.

extracted_variables.speed: speed of the bicycle in meters per second

solution_template.explain: Multiply the minutes by 60 to convert them into seconds.
Multiply speed by the time in seconds to find the distance in meters.
